subject: Capacity mediation: CeruleanAI / AtlasData dedicated GPU scheduling
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@ceruleanai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ceruleanai.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — CeruleanAI pilot

Hi Ben,

Following our R&D sync, Cerulean is ready to move our pilot to dedicated capacity. Target go-live window: week of Jan 18, 2027. Initial sizing: ~3–5 A100-equivalent GPUs; expected steady concurrency ~12 sessions, spike concurrency up to ~45 during batch scoring, average seq lengths ~2k tokens.

Can you confirm availability and provide an SOW + lead time? We also need a clear escalation path if capacity contention arises — we expect the pilot to be revenue-producing within 30 days of launch.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of ML Engineering
CeruleanAI

Attachment: 2026-11-29_Cerulean_sizing_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ceruleanai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — CeruleanAI pilot

Samir — thanks for the details. We can support the pilot but want to flag a potential overlap with another customer (AtlasData) who has an approved Q1 reserved start in the same geography and week.

Initial proposal: reserve 3 A100-class GPUs (guaranteed) + 2 burst slots (best-effort) for Cerulean, with guaranteed burst windows for peak batch scoring (2x 2-hour windows per day). Estimated monthly committed cost and SOW attached.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm acceptance of the 3+2 model and the tentative Jan 18 start.
- I’ll coordinate with capacity ops to lock the dates and define escalation/priority rules.

I’m looping in Vivek to advise on allocation options.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SOW_Cerulean_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — CeruleanAI pilot (allocation conflict)

Team — heads-up: Cerulean intends to start a paid pilot week of Jan 18. AtlasData (deal ATL-202610-3) has an approved Q1 reserved start for Jan 12 (4 A100s) in the same US-west cluster. Both deals are signed-ish (AtlasData signed PO; Cerulean expects to sign after SOW confirmation).

Quick facts:
- AtlasData ARR/commit: ~$95k/month (PO confirmed)
- Cerulean expected ARR/commit: ~$45k/month (SOW pending; revenue will ramp quickly if pilot converts)
- Both require low-tail latency; neither requested multi-region fallback yet.

Can we surface the options and recommend a policy? Possible approaches: honor PO first-come-first-served; carve fixed reserved for Atlas and offer Cerulean burst windows; or time-slice nodes for both during the first 30 days.

Need a decision by EOD Monday so we can share a definitive start date.

— Ben
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — CeruleanAI pilot (allocation conflict)

Thanks for flagging. My recommendation: apply the signed-commit precedence with a short-term mediation window for high-value pilots. Specifics:

1) AtlasData: honor the PO — they get 4 reserved A100s starting Jan 12.
2) CeruleanAI: offer a hybrid plan — 2 reserved A100s guaranteed + 2 burst-capable preemptible slots, with guaranteed burst windows (00:00–02:00 PT and 12:00–14:00 PT) to cover batch scoring. After 30 days, if Cerulean signs a committed reserved plan we can re-evaluate allocations.
3) Implement a temporary throttling policy for best-effort burst slots: preemption order based on signed commit > SOW-signed > self-serve.

Operational tasks:
- Marcus to schedule the cluster carve and tag reservations.
- Rishi to update routing and burst-preemption rules.
- Lauren to draft customer-facing email describing the mediation outcome and escalation path.

I’ll stand by to approve once ops confirms feasibility.

— Vivek
Director, Dedicated Capacity Ops
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ceruleanai.com>, procurement@ceruleanai.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Allocation plan and next steps for Jan pilot

Samir — thanks for your patience while we worked this through internally. We have a mediation outcome that balances both customers' go-lives:

Summary (final):
- CeruleanAI: 2 reserved A100-class GPUs + 2 burst-capable preemptible slots. Two guaranteed 2-hour burst windows daily (00:00–02:00 PT and 12:00–14:00 PT).
- AtlasData: 4 reserved A100-class GPUs starting Jan 12 (honor PO).
- Burst preemption priority: Atlas (PO) > Cerulean (SOW signed) > self-serve.

Next steps for Cerulean:
1) Review and sign the attached SOW by Dec 14 to secure the hybrid reservation.
2) Confirm preferred burst windows (defaults proposed above).
3) Notify us within 24 hours if you need multi-region failover — that’s an add-on.

If you accept we’ll lock the cluster carve and provide an operational runbook and escalation contact (on-call + manager).

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

One ask: can we have a 24/7 on-call number for the first 14 days post-launch in case we observe unexpected preemptions during peak scoring? If that’s straightforward to add to the runbook, we’ll include it in our acceptance.
